Level 1 · Understand

Level 1: Agentic Cybersecurity Foundations

The disciplined baseline: security principles, how agents are built, and the first threat model you can defend.

Open the live courseSee pathways

Core lessons live; bridge and assessment in design

Who it is for
Career changers, junior security practitioners, developers moving into security, and technical managers who need a baseline they can reason from.
Before you start
None. An entry diagnostic decides whether a short networking, operating-systems or programming bridge comes first.
Capstone evidence
Foundational knowledge exam, a safe lab practical and a basic threat model of a small agent.
How it is assessed
Blueprint-balanced knowledge items plus one observed lab task. Knowledge alone never earns the level.

Modules and evidence

Each module ends in an artefact that goes into your portfolio.

ModuleYou will be able toEvidence
Cybersecurity principles for agentic systemsApply CIA, safety, trust boundaries, assets, threat, vulnerability and risk; explain defence in depth and shared responsibility.Asset inventory and security boundary map
Agentic system anatomyDescribe models, orchestration, tools, context, memory, retrieval, identity, execution and multi-agent workflows.Annotated architecture and data-flow diagram
Networking, operating systems and cloud essentialsExplain protocols, segmentation, endpoint security, containers, cloud responsibility, logging and secrets.Hardened baseline and network trust map
Identity, access and cryptographyDistinguish authentication from authorisation; apply least privilege, workload identity, key lifecycle and delegation.Permission matrix and identity flow
Secure software and supply-chain foundationsRun a threat model; apply secure SDLC, dependency hygiene, build integrity and vulnerability handling.Threat model and secure build checklist
AI-specific threats and prompt injectionRecognise untrusted context, direct and indirect injection, tool misuse, poisoning and exfiltration.Attack tree and mitigation plan in an isolated lab
Governance, risk and incident responseKeep a risk register with owners; follow the response lifecycle; preserve evidence.Risk register, incident runbook and tabletop
Integrated secure-agent caseApply the fundamentals to a small customer-support or internal-operations agent.Portfolio submission and timed practical

Planned lessons

These lessons are not written yet. They close gaps found in the audit.

  • P9Foundations bridge: networks, operating systems, cloud and cryptography Planned
    A short bridge for learners who arrive without networking, operating-systems or cryptography fundamentals, so Level 1 does not assume them.
  • P11The Secure Agentic Enterprise Dossier: building the portfolio Planned
    The single evolving portfolio the academy uses as evidence: templates, validation, versioning and export, introduced at Level 1 and extended at every level.
